question: The events in Ceuta in July 2026 confirmed a pattern. The mass storming of an external border is no longer a spontaneous event. It is organised, timed and aimed at the seams of European law. It constitutes a third type of instrumentalisation, alongside coercive state action and corrosive grey zone pressure. Member States have been left to improvise.

Finland adopted an emergency law because the EU had not written any rules. Spain applies a different framework. Twenty-seven national emergency fixes are not a system. They are 27 court cases waiting to happen, and every divergence is a seam our adversaries will test. 1.

Will the Commission bring forward a legislative package establishing a single EU legal category and a single border procedure for organised mass storming situations, which is fast, lawful, and applicable at all external borders?
How does the Commission assess the fragmentation risk that divergent national emergency laws pose to the Schengen area and to uniform fundamental rights protection?
What is the Commission’s timetable for closing this legislative gap within the current mandate?
